home.problemHeading: Your process document is not your process.
home.problemLead: The real one has rework loops, people chasing each other for answers, and long stretches where a case just waits. A request can sit in a queue for days and need only minutes of actual work. Automate the documented version and you automate the wrong thing.
home.problemKicker: The waiting is the process. The work is minutes.
home.discoveryHeading: How we find the real process
home.discoveryLead: We look at the work from three sides, because each one shows something the others miss.

discovery.title: Interviews: the why
discovery.body: We talk to the people who do the work: who decides, which workarounds they rely on, and the thresholds nobody wrote down.

discovery.title: Your systems' logs: the what
discovery.body: Your ERP, CRM and helpdesk record every case, so we can see how many arrive, how long each step takes, where cases wait and which ones loop back.

discovery.title: Everything else
discovery.body: Procedures, spreadsheets, email threads and chat hold the exceptions and rules your systems never captured.

home.bucketsLead: In that order. Most teams start with the model.

buckets.title: Delete
buckets.body: Steps that exist because of an old workaround, a duplicate check or a report nobody reads. A deleted step costs nothing to run.

buckets.title: Plain code
buckets.body: Steps with fixed rules: copy this field, send that reminder, match these two amounts. Ordinary software does them reliably and cheaply.

buckets.title: An agent
buckets.body: Steps that need reading and judgement within clear limits, such as an unstructured email, a mismatched invoice or a missing document. The agent prepares the case.

buckets.title: A person
buckets.body: Decisions with consequences: approvals, exceptions and negotiations. The agent hands them over with the context attached, and a person makes the call.

home.stepsLead: You give us access to the work and the people who do it. We do the mapping, the building and the measuring.

steps.title: Map the real process
steps.body: Interviews, system logs and documents show how the work really moves, including the loops and the waiting.

steps.title: Set the baseline
steps.body: Before we build anything, we measure volume, cycle time, waiting time and exceptions, so the result can be compared with today.

steps.title: Sort and build
steps.body: We delete what shouldn't exist, write plain code for the fixed rules and build agents for the steps that need judgement. Each process has one owner on your side.

steps.title: Measure and expand
steps.body: We measure the same numbers again. Once the process holds, we move on to the next one.

home.systemsHeading: Built on the systems you already run
home.systemsLead: You keep your ERP, your CRM and your helpdesk. Agents connect to them and work by your rules.

systems.title: Connected to your stack
systems.body: Agents work through the APIs of your ERP, CRM, helpdesk and data platforms, with only the permissions you grant.

systems.title: A person makes the call
systems.body: Agents prepare each case and stop at the decision. Approvals and exceptions go to the person who owns them.

systems.title: A record of every action
systems.body: Every decision and change is logged, so your team and your auditors can see what happened and why.

about.heading: Working with AI since before ChatGPT.
body: I run the agency. Well before ChatGPT, I started an AI company that automated fraud and security work, and later kept building AI at a company in San Francisco.

Those years taught us most of what we know: how a process actually works once you look closely, which steps a person should keep, and what still works months after launch. We tried new things early, and plenty of them didn't work the first time.
That's what we bring to your team. We've seen processes of all kinds, and every project starts the same way: sitting down with the people who do the work and learning how it really runs.

home.faqHeading: Questions we hear on first calls

faqs.q: What happens on the discovery call?
faqs.a: We pick one process and map how it really runs: who touches it, where cases wait and where they loop back. You leave with a first view of which steps to delete, which to automate and which to keep with a person, whether or not we work together.

faqs.q: How long until the first agent is live?
faqs.a: It depends on the process and how many systems it touches. We agree a timeline once the process is mapped, and we set the baseline before we build anything.

faqs.q: What can the agents actually do?
faqs.a: They read documents and messages, update your systems, check each case against your rules and gather the evidence for a decision. Then they stop and hand the decision to a person, with the context attached.

faqs.q: Do the agents work with the tools we already have?
faqs.a: Yes. They connect through APIs to ERPs, CRMs, helpdesks, databases and data platforms, so you keep the systems your team knows.

faqs.q: How much of our team's time will it take?
faqs.a: Most of it comes at the start, in interviews about how the work really runs, followed by short reviews of the design. We do the building and the running.

faqs.q: How do you handle security and data?
faqs.a: Agents run inside your existing permissions and security policies, and every action is logged and auditable. We can work under your data processing agreement.

faqs.q: How do you know it worked?
faqs.a: We measure the process before we build: volume, cycle time, waiting time and exceptions. After launch we measure the same things again and show you the comparison.
It depends on the complexity of the workflow, the systems involved and the scope of the deployment. After the discovery call we send you a written proposal.
